description_full: Arxis, Inc. designs and manufactures electronic and mechanical components for mission critical applications in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Electronic Components and Mechanical Components. Its Electronic Components segment provides engineered electronic components and interconnect solutions, including connectors, cable assemblies, microelectronic packaging, radio frequency (RF) and microwave products, power products, sensors, capacitors. and resistors. The Mechanical Components segment offers precision and self-lubricating bearings, seals, springs, gaskets and ducting, and radar absorbing materials. It serves defense and space systems, commercial aerospace platforms, medical technology, semiconductor testing, analytical devices, industrial automation, and other specialized industrial sectors. The company was founded in 2019 and is based in Bloomfield, Connecticut.

financial_summary: Arxis, Inc. is a large-cap industrials business with a $21.5B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +94% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -3.0pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 2% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 46%.
The business throws off $209M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.7%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
